text.p: LME nickel spiralled lower, breaching successive layers of support on disappointed liquidation and technical selling, traders said. The others were less energetic after a three-day weekend with aluminium drifting off its highs and copper consolidating at easier levels.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index fell 0.59 points to 250.72.

On the LME, three months nickel dived after several days of weak performances unnerved long players, ending the afternoon kerb $229 lower at $7,301. As longs sold off positions, prices broke through trendline support at $7,400 and triggered further technical selling, analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff said.
Three months aluminium jogged to a $1,658 per tonne peak early in the morning on speculative buying, but spent the rest of the day meandering down when fresh buying failed to emerge.
Prices finished the afternoon just $3 firmer at $1,636.
Copper took a rest after last week's fresh highs, hovering above $2,500. It finished $13 lower at $2,507 after trading between $2,517 and $2,504.
Other metals finished barely different after sluggish trade. Tin ended $20 higher at $5,730, lead was $1 firmer at $634 and last business in zinc was $3 off at $1,360.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on rain over the weekend in the U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat region, traders said. "In wheat, it was weather plus disappointing exports for wheat and we're not that far away from new crop harvest," said Joe Victor, analyst for Allendale Inc. Wheat closed three to 14-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with July down 11-1/2 at $3.63-1/2 a bushel.

New York precious metals ended firmer Tuesday as markets reopened after the Memorial Day holiday, with a surge in platinum and palladium helping to boost the complex and gold shrugging off latest Bundesbank revaluation announcements, dealers said. COMEX June gold settled $1.60 higher at $344.70 an ounce, traded $345.30 to $344.00. Volume was estimated at 51,000 lots, but much of this was due to rollover from the June contract to August, ahead of the first delivery day on Friday, dealers said.

NYMEX crude oil futures prices ended sharply lower Tuesday after traders returned from a long weekend to find a market bulging with speculative long positions, a clear signal to sell, traders said. Unleaded gasoline and heating oil prices also tumbled. July crude oil lost 84 cents to settle at $20.79 a barrel, after dropping to a low of $20.65 from its high of $21.57, where it opened.
